message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it’s handled through the city’s public‑safety and code‑enforcement offices rather than the city council itself.**  
Below is a quick guide on how to do it, who to contact, and what to expect.

---

## 1. Where to File a Noise Complaint

| Channel | How to Use | Contact Info |
|---------|------------|--------------|
| **Atlanta 311 (Phone & Text)** | Call **404‑656‑3111** or text “NOISE” to 311. The dispatcher will route your call to the appropriate department. | 404‑656‑3111 (phone) / 404‑656‑3111 (text) |
| **Online Portal** | Visit the City of Atlanta’s 311 website and select “Noise Complaint.” You’ll be prompted to fill out a short form. | https://311.atlantaga.gov/ |
| **Email** | Send a detailed description of the noise issue to **noise@atlantaga.gov**. Include location, time, and any evidence (photos, audio clips). | noise@atlantaga.gov |
| **In‑Person** | Drop by the **Department of Public Safety – Code Enforcement** office at 101 West Peachtree Street, Atlanta, GA 30303. | 404‑656‑3111 (office) |
| **City Council Member** | If the issue is persistent or you want a council member to intervene, contact your local council member’s office. They can refer you to the right department. | Find your council member here: https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/council |

---

## 2. What Happens After You File

1. **Initial Assessment** – A dispatcher or code‑enforcement officer will review your complaint and determine if it falls under the city’s noise ordinance.
2. **Investigation** – If the complaint is valid, an officer may visit the site to record noise levels and verify the violation.
3. **Enforcement** – Depending on the severity, the city can issue a warning, a citation, or, in extreme cases, order a temporary shutdown of the source of the noise.
4. **Follow‑Up** – You’ll receive a case number and can track the status online or by calling 311.

---

## 3. Atlanta’s Noise Ordinance (Key Points)

| Time | Allowed Decibel Level | Typical Violations |
|------|-----------------------|--------------------|
| **Weekdays 7 am–10 pm** | 55 dB (typical residential) | Loud music, construction, barking dogs |
| **Weekdays 10 pm–7 am** | 45 dB | Night‑time parties, loud engines |
| **Weekends & Holidays** | 55 dB (7 am–10 pm) | Same as weekdays |
| **Special Events** | 65 dB (with permit) | Concerts, festivals (requires permit) |

*The city’s code enforcement office will reference the specific sections of the Atlanta Municipal Code (Title 12, Chapter 12.1) when assessing violations.*

---

## 4. Tips for a Successful Complaint

- **Be Specific**: Include exact address, dates, times, and a description of the noise source.
- **Provide Evidence**: Attach photos, audio recordings, or witness statements if possible.
- **Check the Ordinance**: Knowing the exact decibel limits helps you explain why the noise is a violation.
- **Follow Up**: Use the case number to check status; if no action is taken within a reasonable timeframe, call 311 again.

---

## 5. Quick Links

- **Atlanta 311 Portal**: https://311.atlantaga.gov/
- **Noise Ordinance (PDF)**: https://www.atlantaga.gov/sites/default/files/Noise%20Ordinance.pdf
- **City Council Contact Page**: https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/council
- **Department of Public Safety – Code Enforcement**: https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/department-of-public-safety

---

### Bottom Line

You can definitely report a noise complaint in Atlanta. Use the 311 system (phone, text, or online), email, or visit the code‑enforcement office. The city council can help if the issue escalates, but the primary enforcement body is the Department of Public Safety’s Code Enforcement division.
